messages:
tess.sales: Customer (ShopQuick tenant=shopq-445) hitting intermittent 429s when importing embeddings. Demo in 3 hours, theyre blocked.

ravi-eng: Which endpoint and concurrency? Any sample error payload?

tess.sales: /v1/embeddings, client is firing ~80 concurrent tiny batches (many 1-item calls). Error: 
`{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","code":429},"request_id":"cafebabe-01"}`

mei-sre: Pulled logs for cafebabe-01: 
`[2026-05-10T14:05:12Z] ratecap=DENY tenant=shopq-445 route=/v1/embeddings reason=PER_ROUTE_REQ_WINDOW matched=60s allowed=50 reqs=51 req_id=cafebabe-01`

ravi-eng: So they hit the per-route reqs window (50/min). Two options: ask client to batch larger/fewer concurrent calls, or apply short-lived per-route bump. Also check daily token budget.

billing-bot: NOTICE: shopq-445 today_tokens=1,750,000 / daily_limit=2,000,000 (87%).

tess.sales: Customer cannot change client before demo. Can we do a temporary bump + a config to coalesce small requests for trials?

mei-sre: We can enable `coalesce_small_requests=true` for this tenant and set per_route_req cap->200 for 2 hours. But billing must sign off on potential token overage.

ravi-eng: I'll toggle coalesce now (low-risk). Command: `rb config set shopq-445 coalesce_small_requests true`

mei-sre: Coalesce applied. Now awaiting billing.

billing-bot: APPROVED: temporary per-route increase to 200 reqs/min for tenant shopq-445 until 2026-05-10T16:05:12Z. Token buffer not applied.

tess.sales: Customer reports 429s dropped to near-zero. Demo is back on. Please add a short note to the sales playbook about preferring batch sizes >=8 and including token_count hint.

ravi-eng: Will add a 1-paragraph guidance. Also follow-up: consider surfacing more explicit 429 reasons in payload (per-route vs token-budget).

mei-sre: Noted. Closing the incident.
